item.title: Xi urges strong steps to build Healthy China
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-14
Xi urges strong steps to build Healthy China Health: Application of research highlighted President Xi Jinping has called for continuous efforts to improve people's health and secure decisive progress in the development of the Healthy China Initiative over the 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-30) period. Xi, who is also general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, made the remarks at a national meeting on health, which was held in Beijing on Monday and Tuesday. He underlined the need to firmly follow a path with Chinese characteristics in developing the country's healthcare programs, and to leverage strengths and address weak links in order to promote the high-quality development of the health sector. People's health is a crucial hallmark of a nation's prosperity and strength, Xi said, emphasizing the CPC Central Committee's strategic decision to promote the Healthy China Initiative. Since the 18th National Congress of the CPC in late 2012, the Party Central Committee, with Xi at the core, has given strategic priority to ensuring people's health. It made the major decision to advance the Healthy China Initiative nationwide. The initiative, which aims to improve public health and promote healthier lifestyles, covers areas such as public health services, environmental management, the development of the healthcare industry, and food and drug safety. It is part of the country's broader efforts to address the challenges posed by an aging population, the increasing prevalence of chronic diseases, and the rising costs of healthcare. From targeted advances in key areas to nationwide coverage of inclusive health services that meet basic needs, China, with a population of more than 1.4 billion, has blazed a path of health development with its own characteristics. It has established the world's largest medical service system, traditional medicine service system, disease prevention and control system, and medical security system. China aims to establish a health system by 2035 that is compatible with a society that has basically achieved modernization. Xi emphasized at the meeting that the Healthy China that the country strives to build should provide balanced, inclusive, high-quality and efficient medical and healthcare services. It should possess strong capabilities in health management, disease prevention and control, medical services, medical insurance support, innovation and talent development, and should effectively meet the growing demands of people regarding health, with major health indicators steadily improving, he said. Highlighting its holistic and fundamental role, Xi called for prioritizing the development of healthcare. Health considerations should be integrated into policies and reflected in all areas of work, including planning, policy design, project evaluation and construction, he added. Xi stressed that improving medical services is a key task in building a Healthy China, and he called for concrete measures, including optimizing the layout of medical institutions and tiered diagnosis and treatment, to ensure that people can access medical care close to home and receive effective treatment. Efforts should be made to optimize medical services to the satisfaction of the people, he added. Thanks to continuous efforts throughout society over the past decades, the vision of ensuring that serious illnesses can be treated within one's home provincial-level region, common illnesses within one's city or county, and everyday ailments at the grassroots level is increasingly becoming a reality. China has supported the development of 125 national regional medical centers so far, with 75 percent of their hospitals located in central and western regions and other areas where high-quality medical resources are relatively scarce, Xinhua News Agency reported. More than 90 percent of residents can access nearby medical and healthcare services within 15 minutes. Primary-level medical institutions account for more than 50 percent of all medical visits nationwide. Coordinated development and governance of healthcare services, medical insurance and pharmaceuticals have helped reduce out-of-pocket payments to 27.1 percent of total health expenditure. A range of health indicators point to improvements in the country's overall health status. In 2025, China's average life expectancy was 79.25 years, while its major health indicators remained at a leading position among upper-middle-income countries and countries with a population exceeding 100 million. The premature mortality rate from major chronic diseases fell to 13.8 percent, and major infectious diseases and endemic diseases were effectively brought under control. During the meeting, Xi called for intensifying basic research and original innovation in the medical and healthcare sector and promoting the transformation of technological research achievements into applications to strengthen the healthcare industry. China is producing a growing range of domestically developed drugs, medical equipment, vaccines, medical consumables and approaches to diagnosis and treatment. In the first half of 2026 alone, the nation approved 38 innovative drugs for market entry, according to a Xinhua report. Xi also urged reform in the medical and healthcare sector, saying that the coordinated development and governance of medical services, medical insurance and pharmaceuticals should be the primary focus in reforming the healthcare system. Noting that ensuring health for all is a common vision for humanity, he called for actively promoting the building of a global community of health for all, jointly addressing major challenges in public health, and continuously improving the health and well-being of people worldwide.

item.title: Art of making Yangzhou fried rice draws diners in
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-14
At first glance, the fried rice dish looks like a simple combination of rice, eggs, shrimp and vegetables. However, in Yangzhou, Jiangsu province, preparing the city's signature dish requires careful ingredient selection, precise timing and control of the wok. For Russian student Vladyslav Shlykov, the attention to detail came as a surprise when his Chinese classmates took him to try Yangzhou fried rice on a recent trip. Watching the chef at work, he was struck by the variety of ingredients used and the precision of each movement, from the order in which ingredients were added to the wok to the timing of each step. The taste impressed him just as much. "I would be very happy to recommend Yangzhou fried rice to my friends," he said. This seemingly simple dish has a culinary tradition behind it, built on careful ingredient selection and precise cooking techniques. "It is not simply a way to use up leftover rice. It is a carefully prepared dish in which rice and other ingredients come together as a complete meal," said Xia Chaobing, a Chinese culinary master and inheritor of the dish's traditional preparation techniques. One defining technique is known as "silver wrapped in gold", referring to egg coating the rice. To achieve this effect, chefs must select rice grains of a consistent size and use the correct proportion of egg. Xia usually adds the egg in two stages to ensure an even coating. The freshness of the eggs is also crucial. According to Xia, the eggs used for Yangzhou fried rice should be no more than five days old. As eggs age, their whites become less viscous, which makes it harder for the egg mixture to coat the rice grains evenly. Rice selection also matters. Even the same variety can produce different textures from one batch to another, so chefs need to test the rice and adjust their methods accordingly. Chefs must also control the heat and work quickly to prevent the rice from sticking to the wok. A typical version combines rice and eggs with diced bamboo shoots, shiitake mushrooms, green peas, shrimp, shrimp roe, sea cucumber, dried scallops, diced chicken and diced Jinhua ham. Once the rice and other ingredients have been prepared in advance, Xia said that the actual cooking takes about 12 to 13 minutes. The preparation techniques for Yangzhou fried rice were inscribed on the list of intangible cultural heritage of Jiangsu in 2009. According to Xu Yinghong, vice-president of the Jiangsu Catering Association, the dish reflects the Huaiyang culinary tradition's focus on selecting the finest ingredients, precise preparation and controlled heat. Yangzhou's location along the Grand Canal has shaped its culinary culture over centuries of trade and exchange. The city developed a food tradition that values technical precision and harmony among ingredients. Yangzhou fried rice has also found an international audience. Xu recalled visiting Brazil in 2019 and finding the dish on the menus of Chinese restaurants in Rio de Janeiro and Sao Paulo. He attributes its overseas popularity partly to Chinese communities introducing familiar dishes abroad and partly to its versatility. By combining rice, vegetables, eggs and meat or seafood in one dish, Yangzhou fried rice can appeal to diners from a variety of culinary backgrounds. Xia said that the recipe had been adapted for Muslim diners by replacing the ham with beef and adding carrots. For first-time visitors, Xia offers three suggestions: Eat the fried rice while it is hot, use a spoon to gather different ingredients in each mouthful, and chew slowly to appreciate how the individual flavors complement one another. In Yangzhou, visitors can explore the wider cultural context of the dish beyond the dining table. They can watch chefs demonstrate their skills at time-honored establishments such as Fuchun and Yechun, visit the China Grand Canal Museum and the Huaiyang Cuisine Museum of China, or sample the city's celebrated morning tea.

item.title: Flowing with AI's growth highlighted at skills event
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-14
Flowing with AI's growth highlighted at skills event Participants in global competition focus on utilizing new tech, upgrading capabilities Qiu Mengying, 25, is confident that her aircraft engineer job is indispensable and has no fear she will be replaced by intelligent machines. Despite heated debate over the threat to the workforce posed by artificial intelligence, Qiu, a member of an aircraft maintenance training team that participated in the recent 48th WorldSkills Competition, said: "In our profession, AI is just a helper. It is not here to replace us." The seven skills added to this year's event, which concluded in Shanghai on Sept 27, are unique and hard to automate, she added. "These new skills reflect the latest trends in occupational development and industrial upgrading," said Qiu, while demonstrating her aircraft maintenance skills at the China Eastern Airlines exhibition booth. "They send a signal to more students and young people about where career opportunities are headed, while helping them gain a clearer understanding of their own career plans." Future requirements Unlike many standardized and repetitive jobs, the new skills included in the competition offered a glimpse of the expertise workers will need as industries transform and develop. Known as a bellwether of industrial upgrades and employment trends, WorldSkills Shanghai 2026 helped shed light on "irreplaceable occupations" despite AI's spread, said officials and participants. The skills look to tap into the core employment requirements of digitalization, multidisciplinary and specialized skills. They send clear signals that despite the overwhelming application of AI across various cutting-edge sectors — including digital economy, smart infrastructure and modern commerce — humans cannot be replaced by intelligent machines, the officials and participants said. "There are a total of 64 skills at this year's competition, including seven new skills appearing at the event for the first time," Wu Liduo, director general of occupational capacity building at the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security, said during a State Council Information Office news conference in Beijing in June.

item.title: Shanghai wins inaugural city of innovation award
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-13
Shanghai wins inaugural city of innovation award Award: Executives praise Shanghai's AI advances In recognition of its ability to leverage intellectual property rights to drive innovation, protect ideas and scale solutions, Shanghai has been declared one of the winners of the first WIPO City of Innovation award, which was announced by the World Intellectual Property Organization on Monday. The other winners of the inaugural edition of the award from among 15 finalist cities are Liverpool in the United Kingdom and Charleroi in Belgium. According to the WIPO, Shanghai has been recognized by an independent international jury for expanding IP education and services, opening innovation infrastructure and data, supporting cultural and creative industries, and strengthening connections between research, industry, entrepreneurs and investors. Daren Tang, director-general of the WIPO, said that today, more than half of humanity lives in cities, a figure projected to reach 70 percent by 2050. "As urban populations surge, cities bring together people with different backgrounds, skills, experiences and aspirations, often sparking and stimulating new ideas. But true innovation demands ecosystems where IP protects new ideas, empowers innovators and enables solutions to scale from concept to reality," he said. Zhou Yaming, deputy secretary-general of the Shanghai Municipal People's Government, said the award represents the WIPO's strong recognition of Shanghai's innovative developments and its efforts to build a thriving IP ecosystem. "It also reflects the international community's endorsement of China's commitment to open innovation, mutual benefits and shared success," Zhou said in an interview with Xinhua News Agency. Multinational companies operating in Shanghai have long been impressed by the level and speed of innovation in the city. Stefan Paul, CEO of Swiss logistics giant Kuehne+Nagel, said Shanghai mirrors the ongoing progress in China, with the level of digitalization and automation and the speed of innovation being"second to none". According to Bjoern Gulden, CEO of Adidas AG, the sportswear brand has a team of 160 designers working in Shanghai, which has autonomy in design and product development. A local team can significantly reduce development time and respond quickly to new consumer demands, he said. Gulden added that Shanghai means more for the company. As an international hub for talents, universities and high-consumption activities, Shanghai is integral to the global expansion plans of Adidas. Therefore, the company will combine local consumption data with state-of-the-art technologies such as artificial intelligence to apply insights to manufacturing and new materials, he said. Multinational manufacturing conglomerate ABB also applauded Shanghai's pioneering efforts in the field of AI. Morten Wierod, the company's CEO, is impressed by the city's AI ecosystem covering computing power, models and applications. Shanghai's ongoing digital and AI innovation will power its leap to become a "city of the future", he said. Roland Busch, CEO of Siemens AG, said that Shanghai has gained an upper hand in applying AI in innovative industrial service scenarios. Along with integrated circuits and biomedicine, AI has been defined as one of the three leading industries in Shanghai since 2020. The manufacturing output value of the three industries grew 14.5 percent year-on-year in the first half of 2026. In the first six months, Shanghai's AI manufacturing output grew 21.8 percent year-on-year, and 1,945 AI invention patents were granted, up 64.79 percent from a year earlier. The municipal government has been planning ahead. In September 2024, the municipal government launched a fund to support the development of six future-oriented industries — manufacturing, information technology, materials, energy, space and healthcare. Fully backed by the government fiscal budget, the fund's initial scale stood at 10 billion yuan ($1.5 billion). The six industries have been included in Shanghai's 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-30) as part of its modern industrial framework. According to John Waldron, president and chief operating officer of Goldman Sachs, attracting the world's best talents is crucial to sustaining Shanghai's innovation and growth momentum. The city should invest more resources to make the lives of residents more convenient, he added.

item.title: Xiangjiang River Battle spirit fuels village's rural vitalization
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-13
Xiangjiang River Battle spirit fuels rural vitalization in Quanzhou, Guangxi More than 90 years ago, during the Long March, the Central Red Army fought a desperate battle against Kuomintang troops along the Xiangjiang River. At tremendous cost, the army broke through the enemy's fourth blockade line and preserved the revolutionary spark. The Xiangjiang River Battle forged a spirit of daring to win and daring to break through. Today, Nanyi village in Quanzhou county, Guangxi Zhuang autonomous region, has taken up this spiritual torch. Quanzhou county is one of the sites of the Xiangjiang River Battle. Wang Junrong, Party secretary of Nanyi village, returned to his hometown to lead efforts to develop the grape industry in Maozhushan village, which is administered by Nanyi. By improving grape varieties, extending the picking season, using livestreaming to sell grapes and attracting tourists, the village and its residents have greatly benefited. As always, the revolutionary legacy has played a key role as a driving force on this new journey.

item.title: China, Togo elevate bilateral ties
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-13
China, Togo elevate bilateral ties President Xi Jinping on Tuesday put forward a series of key principles for the constructive participation of all parties in the settlement of hot-spot issues in Africa, stressing that the African people are the true masters of Africa and should play a central role in regional affairs. He made the remarks while meeting in Beijing with Faure Essozimna Gnassingbe, president of the Council of the Togolese Republic, who is on an eight-day official visit to China running through Friday. During the meeting, the two leaders elevated bilateral relations to a China-Togo community with a shared future for the new era. Elaborating on the principles, Xi emphasized upholding fairness and justice, and urged all relevant parties to abide by the purposes and principles of the United Nations Charter and respect the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the countries concerned. Noting that wars and unilateral sanctions cannot truly resolve differences between countries, he said that it is imperative to uphold mutual respect, conduct extensive consultations, seek common ground while shelving differences, and practice mutual understanding and accommodation. Xi also emphasized the importance of addressing both symptoms and root causes. Efforts should focus on immediate security while planning for long-term development, he said. Gnassingbe said that Togo fully agrees with the principles proposed by Xi, and highly commends China's key role in safeguarding world peace and stability and jointly addressing global challenges. Togo is ready to strengthen multilateral cooperation with China, jointly defend multilateralism and uphold the interests of developing countries, he added. On bilateral relations, Xi called on the two countries to further strengthen exchanges at all levels, deepen the sharing of governance experience and firmly support each other on issues concerning their respective core interests and major concerns. Togo is welcome to make good use of China's zero-tariff treatment and the green lanes for African products exported to China, and further leverage its role as a regional trade and logistics hub, so as to bring more distinctive products from Togo and the region into the Chinese market, he said. Xi expressed appreciation for Togo's efforts to expand cross-border use of the renminbi, saying that China is ready to strengthen bilateral cooperation in fields such as new energy and digital and smart technologies to support Togo's industrialization. Gnassingbe said that during his visit, he witnessed how China's modernization drive has made remarkable achievements and how fine traditional Chinese culture has been carried forward. Such experiences have given him a better understanding of China's governance philosophy and the sources of its success, Gnassingbe said. Noting that the two countries will celebrate the 55th anniversary of diplomatic ties next year, he expressed Togo's willingness to work with China to enhance mutual trust, strengthen dialogue and communication, and intensify enduring and mutually beneficial cooperation. Before visiting Beijing, Gnassingbe made stops in Shaanxi and Fujian provinces. His itinerary also includes Guangdong province.

item.title: Mining cooperation with Africa highlighted at talks
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-13
Mining cooperation with Africa highlighted at talks President Xi Jinping called on Tuesday for China-Africa mining cooperation to help African countries translate their mineral wealth into development gains to advance the continent's modernization, stressing that those resources belong to Africa and should not become tools of geopolitical rivalry. Xi made the remarks during talks with visiting Botswanan President Duma Gideon Boko at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, where the two leaders announced the elevation of bilateral ties to a comprehensive strategic cooperative partnership. Boko arrived in China on Monday for a six-day state visit, his first since taking office in November 2024. Beijing is the second stop on his itinerary, following a visit to Fujian province in East China with engagements focused on industrial development, technology and investment. The two heads of state witnessed the signing of multiple cooperation documents covering the implementation of the Global Security Initiative, Belt and Road cooperation, green minerals, health and human resources. During the talks, which followed a welcoming ceremony, Xi called on the two countries to write a new chapter in their friendship, saying that it should be as brilliant and enduring as diamonds, Botswana's leading export commodity. Mining cooperation featured prominently in the talks, with Xi putting forward four proposals for advancing cooperation between China and Africa in the sector. Such cooperation must proceed from the premise that Africa's resources belong to Africa, Xi said. China is willing to share its experience and help African countries formulate mining development plans suited to their national conditions, he added. He called for cooperation grounded in fairness and mutual benefit, saying that China would continue to encourage its companies to improve their operational capabilities, transfer green technologies suited to African conditions and advance South-South cooperation in mining. Xi also urged a stronger focus on high-quality development. China will continue to promote greater value addition in China-Africa mining cooperation and explore innovative financing models that are affordable and sustainable to support Africa's modernization, he said. Calling for a fair and open environment for cooperation, Xi said Africa's resources should not become tools of geopolitical rivalry. China welcomes sincere efforts by all parties to support Africa's development and is ready to work with African countries to create more favorable conditions for business investment and operations, he added. On bilateral relations, Xi recalled that Botswana had voted in support of restoring the People's Republic of China's lawful seat in the United Nations in the 1970s, even before the two countries established diplomatic relations. Today, he said, the two sides are advancing together in pursuit of modernization. China supports Botswana in following a development path suited to its national conditions, Xi said. He urged both sides to further improve their framework for economic and trade cooperation and make full use of the opportunities brought by China's zero-tariff treatment for all African countries with which it has diplomatic relations. China is ready to strengthen cooperation with Botswana in the digital economy, agriculture and animal husbandry, and implement smart education projects to support the country's economic and social development, he added. Boko praised China's development achievements under Xi's leadership, saying that its development experience offers valuable lessons for Botswana. He said that Botswana firmly adheres to the one-China principle and opposes separatist attempts for "Taiwan independence" and any interference in China's internal affairs. Botswana welcomes more Chinese companies to invest in the country, he said, expressing readiness to expand Belt and Road cooperation and strengthen ties in industry, agriculture, mining, innovation and digital transformation to deliver more tangible results. He also welcomed the four global initiatives proposed by Xi, saying that they demonstrate the responsibility of a major country at a time of significant global challenges. Botswana is ready to strengthen coordination with China, uphold multilateralism, promote solidarity among developing countries and advance China-Africa cooperation to make global governance more inclusive and representative, he said. China and Botswana established diplomatic relations in January 1975 and upgraded their ties to a strategic partnership in September 2024. Bilateral trade reached $1.22 billion in 2025, up 21.3 percent year-on-year, according to China's Foreign Ministry.
